key_points: Self-hosted, evidence-first PostgreSQL investigations with read-only controls and auditable conclusions
Discovers an approved PostgreSQL schema through a dedicated read-only role; never grants a model direct DB credentials or arbitrary SQL execution
Validates SELECT queries against PostgreSQL AST, table scope, row and time bounds before execution
Derives evidence coverage from source-owned table bindings, so a model cannot self-assert its evidence is sufficient
Records evidence hashes and a local tamper-evident audit chain
Provider choice: deterministic replay by default; Ollama/vLLM via OpenAI-compatible adapter; Anthropic only after explicit egress opt-in
Customizable declarative skills: versioned skill definitions with per-tool bounds that can tighten, never weaken, server policy
Public validation alpha (Apache-2.0), not approved for production or customer data
An Agentic PostgreSQL DBA that monitors, analyzes, and optimizes any PostgreSQL 14-18 database with LLM-powered actions
Covers database monitoring, performance, query optimization, observability, and SRE workflows
Supports AlloyDB, Aurora, Cloud SQL, RDS, and self-hosted PostgreSQL
Written in Go; integrates with Prometheus for observability
Contrast: pg_sage is action-oriented (optimize/monitor), while OpsGraph is investigation-oriented and read-only
Pg-Aiguide covers agentic coding for PostgreSQL — using AI agents to write and manage PostgreSQL code
Represents the 'agentic coding' angle: agents generating SQL and schema changes
Contrast: focuses on code generation, not evidence-first incident investigation
PlayBooks are Jupyter-Notebook-style on-call investigation documents that automate production issue investigation
Doctor Droid bot connects to 15+ observability tools and servers, runs commands and fetches data on alert
PlayBooks are intelligent documents connected to every part of the stack: logs, metrics, database queries, remote commands, container data, custom API calls
Contrast: PlayBooks is a general observability investigation framework; OpsGraph is narrowly scoped to read-only PostgreSQL with a tamper-evident audit chain
Open-source agentic data engineering harness (Show HN, 20 points)
Represents the broader trend of agentic data tooling beyond pure investigation
Contrast: data engineering focus vs OpsGraph's incident-investigation focus

stats.fact: OpsGraph is a public validation alpha released 2026-08-16, Apache-2.0 licensed, written in Python, with topics: ai-agents, incident-response, langgraph, observability, postgresql, read-only, self-hosted

OpsGraph's alpha success criteria: sample investigation completes in under five minutes; a PostgreSQL schema can be reviewed within fifteen minutes; every factual claim opens its exact evidence; unsafe SQL and data-bearing dumps fail closed
OpsGraph enforces at most three SELECT queries per investigation, validated against PostgreSQL AST, policy, row bounds, timeout, and a read-only transaction before execution
OpsGraph's threat model treats prompts, database values, identifiers, comments, logs, uploaded SQL, and playbook text as untrusted; stored prompt injection must remain inert data
pg_sage (an Agentic PostgreSQL DBA) supports PostgreSQL 14-18 and integrates with Prometheus, AlloyDB, Aurora, Cloud SQL, RDS, and self-hosted deployments
Doctor Droid PlayBooks automate investigation across 15+ observability tools and servers, fetching logs, metrics, database queries, remote commands, container data, and custom API calls

angles: The trust problem in agentic database tools: why 'ask the model anything' is dangerous for operational data, and how evidence-first design (read-only roles, AST validation, audit chains) restores operator trust
Read-only by design: how OpsGraph enforces a dedicated read-only PostgreSQL role, bounded SELECT queries, and fail-closed policy so an AI can investigate without write access
Evidence coverage derived from source-owned table bindings, not model self-assertion — the key differentiator that prevents hallucinated 'sufficient evidence' claims
Tamper-evident audit chain: evidence hashes and append-only hash-chained audit events make conclusions reproducible and auditable
Local-first / egress-opt-in: running investigations with Ollama/vLLM loopback so sensitive schema and query data never leaves the host
The alpha boundary and threat model: what a public validation alpha explicitly does NOT do (remediation, writes, dump restore, executable plug-ins) and why that scope discipline matters
Comparison of the agentic PostgreSQL landscape: OpsGraph (investigation, read-only) vs pg_sage (DBA optimization) vs PlayBooks (general observability) vs agentic coding tools
